idea: Give physique entries a delete path (remove the DB row and the storage object, and re-derive the session average) instead of no delete affordance at all.
moment: Static analysis of PhysiqueTracker.jsx found only a pose-fix mutation — no delete anywhere in the file. A wrong, duplicate, or embarrassing upload currently has no in-app way to remove it.
howOften: rare per-upload, but permanent when it happens (39 physique_entries rows on record, 21 in the last 90 days)

idea: Reuse WeighInPrompt's BOUNDS sanity check (lbs 50-700 / kg 25-320, reject-and-show-back rather than silently accept) on the Progress page's own Weight tab input.
moment: The exact same 'a typo is a lie the trend estimator can't detect' guard already exists one component away for the dashboard weigh-in prompt, but the Weight tab in Progress.jsx has no min/max at all on the same write path (useLogWeight).
howOften: any time weight is logged from Progress instead of the dashboard prompt

idea: Make body_weight_entries logging a real DB-level upsert (unique constraint on created_by+recorded_date, or ON CONFLICT) instead of client-side select-then-create/update.
moment: Seven different components call useLogWeight for 'today's weight' (Progress, WeighInModal, WeighInPrompt, MorningCheckin, ProgressContent, StatsSetupModal, Profile) — any two firing close together can both read zero existing rows and both insert, producing duplicate same-day weight entries that skew the trend chart and adaptive TDEE. The code already names this exact risk in a comment, just hasn't closed the race.
howOften: rare in isolation, but the failure mode is silent and permanent (a phantom duplicate weight point) when it happens, and there are 7 possible trigger points

idea: Give water log delete and supplement log delete the same ConfirmDialog (or an undo toast) that weight/measurement/supplement-type delete already have.
moment: Testing the Hydration sub-tab: both per-entry delete (X) buttons are instant, no confirm, no isPending guard — the same inconsistency round 1 found in fuel's food-entry delete.
howOften: any time a mis-logged water or supplement entry needs correcting

idea: Make the Measurements tab upsert-by-date like Weight does (or, if multiple-per-day is intentional for AM/PM readings, add a secondary sort key so 'Latest' is deterministic instead of relying on tie-breaking order from the DB).
moment: Saving twice for the same date inserts two rows with no dedupe, and the history query orders by date only (no created_at tiebreak), so which one displays as 'Latest' isn't guaranteed to be the one just saved.
howOften: currently never — measurements usage.json shows 0 total / 0 last 90 days, so this is dormant risk in an unused feature rather than an active pain point

idea: Add a manual-entry fallback for recovery_metrics (sleep score, HRV, resting HR, etc.) for days the Garmin/Apple Health sync misses.
moment: recovery_metrics is the single most-used body-area table by row count (129 total / 89 last 90 days) but every row comes from sync — RecoveryDetail.jsx is entirely read-only with no manual-entry path found anywhere in the app.
howOften: whenever a sync gap happens (watch not worn, Bluetooth miss, etc.)

idea: Distinguish a personalized water goal from the generic 3000ml fallback in the UI copy (e.g. a small 'estimated' badge) when profile.current_weight is unset.
moment: waterGoalMl() silently substitutes DEFAULT_WATER_GOAL_ML with no visual difference from a real personalized number — someone with no weight on file would have no way to know the goal isn't calculated for them.
howOften: only for accounts without current_weight set — likely rare for Nolan's own account but worth a cheap fix

idea: Give MorningCheckin (readiness/soreness/weigh-in) a reachable path when a workout is already in-progress and today has no engine prescription — either render it alongside the 'tap to continue' banner, or link out to it, instead of suppressing the whole PrescribedSessionCard.
moment: Today.jsx:500 suppresses PrescribedSessionCard (which hosts MorningCheckin) whenever `activeSession && !prescription`. Confirmed at runtime: with the shared test account's leftover in-progress workout session and no prescription today, the check-in form was completely unreachable — no alternate route anywhere in the app (MorningCheckin is only imported by PrescribedSessionCard.jsx). An abandoned/forgotten in-progress session can permanently hide the daily check-in.
howOften: any day with a stale/abandoned in-progress workout session and no fresh prescription — plausible after a forgotten 'started but never finished' workout, which is exactly what happened here from a leftover test session

idea: Have useLogWeight's profile-sync step (current_weight) get reverted or re-derived when the body_weight_entries row it came from is deleted — or at least make the two writes transactional so a failed/rolled-back weigh-in never leaves profile.current_weight out of sync with the entries table.
moment: Confirmed while investigating: after the r1-01 race-condition test (two concurrent weigh-in writes to different components, both syncing profile.current_weight), deleting the resulting duplicate body_weight_entries rows left profile.current_weight pointing at whichever write's value happened to resolve last — a value with no corresponding entries row anymore. Had to be manually restored from baseline.
howOften: any time a weigh-in entry is deleted/corrected after the fact — current_weight silently keeps the stale value

idea: Explicitly allow a typed '0' dose when logging a supplement instead of `parseFloat(dose) || type.default_dose` silently substituting the default.
moment: Confirmed bug (body-r1-06): typing '0' into the dose field and tapping Log records the supplement's default_dose instead of 0, because parseFloat('0') is falsy in JS.
howOften: any time someone deliberately logs a 0 dose (e.g. 'skipped today but wanted a record') — silently records the wrong number instead
